title: Perfect Equilibrium And Undominated Equilibrium
body_html:
Perfect Equilibrium And Undominated Equilibrium

In a finite two-player normal-form game, a Nash equilibrium is perfect if and only if it is undominated, meaning that no strategy in its support is weakly dominated.

For games with more than two players, the corresponding inclusion is strict: perfect equilibrium is a stronger requirement than undominated equilibrium.

References

  • [MFoGT, Prop. 6.5.4] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. In two-player finite normal-form games, perfect equilibrium iff undominated; strict inclusion for more players.
